answer: Give each answer's graders a stake in being independent: after a close, any two graders whose scores matched on unusually many of the same answers share a small penalty unless a randomly chosen audit jury agrees with them too. Honest graders rarely trip it, since their agreement tracks real quality. A ring that scores its members identically keeps paying, because audits expose the gap between its votes and a stranger's. Over time the ring's influence goes hollow, each penalty a ripple that compounds, while independent graders grow steadily like yarrow on open ground.
